desc: Mumbai, formerly Bombay, is the capital of Maharashtra and the financial, commercial, and entertainment capital of India. It is the most populous city in India with a metropolitan population of over 20 million. The city is built on a narrow peninsula on the western coast and comprises seven merged islands. Mumbai is home to the Bombay Stock Exchange, Reserve Bank of India, and Bollywood film industry. The city's iconic landmarks include the Gateway of India, Marine Drive, and the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mumbai is the wealthiest city in India and a major global financial center.
fact: Mumbai is India's financial and entertainment capital with a metro population over 20 million · It is built on seven merged islands on the western coast · It is home to the Bombay Stock Exchange, RBI, and Bollywood · The Gateway of India and CSMT are iconic UNESCO-recognized landmarks

desc: Delhi, the national capital of India, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, with a history spanning over 2,500 years. The National Capital Territory has a population of over 30 million, making it the second-most populous city in the world. Delhi has served as the capital of several empires including the Mughal and British Raj. The city is a treasure trove of historical monuments including the Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, and the India Gate — all UNESCO World Heritage Sites. It is also India's political and administrative center, housing the Parliament and Supreme Court.
fact: Delhi is the national capital, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities at over 2,500 years · It has a population of over 30 million, the second-largest city globally · It was the capital of Mughal and British empires · The Red Fort, Qutub Minar, and Humayun's Tomb are UNESCO World Heritage Sites

desc: Bengaluru, formerly Bangalore, is the capital of Karnataka and India's premier technology hub. Known as the 'Silicon Valley of India,' the city is home to the headquarters of major IT companies, startups, and research institutions including ISRO. The city has a metropolitan population of over 13 million, making it the third-most populous city in India. Bengaluru is known for its pleasant year-round climate, extensive parks including Cubbon Park and Lalbagh Botanical Garden, and its vibrant food and nightlife culture. The city was founded in 1537 by Kempe Gowda and retains historic landmarks like the Bangalore Palace and Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace.
fact: Bengaluru is known as the 'Silicon Valley of India,' India's premier technology hub · It is the capital of Karnataka with a metro population of over 13 million · It is known for its pleasant year-round climate and extensive parks · The city was founded in 1537 by Kempe Gowda

desc: Chennai, formerly Madras, is the capital of Tamil Nadu and the largest cultural and economic hub of South India. It is the fourth-most populous metropolitan area in India with over 11 million people. Chennai is a major center for automobile manufacturing, earning the nickname 'Detroit of India.' The city has a rich cultural heritage with classical music and dance festivals at the iconic Madras Music Academy. Landmarks include the 17th-century St. George Fort, Kapaleeshwarar Temple, and the Marina Beach, one of the longest urban beaches in the world. Chennai is known for its traditional Tamil cuisine, film industry (Kollywood), and thriving IT sector.
fact: Chennai is the capital of Tamil Nadu and the 'Detroit of India' for automobile manufacturing · Marina Beach is one of the longest urban beaches in the world · It is the center of Tamil classical music and dance including the famous Music Academy · Chennai's Kollywood film industry is the second-largest in India

desc: Kolkata, formerly Calcutta, is the capital of West Bengal and the principal cultural and intellectual hub of eastern India. With a metropolitan population of over 15 million, it is the third-most populous city in India. Founded as a trading post by the British East India Company in 1690, Kolkata served as the capital of British India until 1911. The city is known for its colonial-era architecture, including the Victoria Memorial, Howrah Bridge, and the Marble Palace. Kolkata is famous for its literary heritage, film industry (Tollywood), and iconic street food. The city is a major center for education and research, hosting prestigious institutions including Presidency University and the Indian Statistical Institute.
fact: Kolkata served as the capital of British India until 1911, founded as a British trading post in 1690 · The Victoria Memorial and Howrah Bridge are iconic city landmarks · It is the cultural and literary capital of eastern India with a metro population of 15 million · Kolkata's Tollywood film industry and street food culture are nationally famous

desc: Hyderabad is the capital of Telangana and one of India's premier pharmaceutical and IT hubs. The city has a rich historical heritage as the seat of the Nizams of Hyderabad and is known for its distinctive fusion of Hindu and Islamic architecture. Landmarks include the iconic Charminar, the Golconda Fort, and the Chowmahalla Palace. Hyderabad is famous for its Hyderabadi biryani and pearl trade, earning it the nickname 'City of Pearls.' The city has a population of over 10 million and is home to major tech campuses including Microsoft, Google, and Amazon. The HITEC City area is a thriving IT corridor that has transformed Hyderabad into a global technology destination.
fact: Hyderabad was the seat of the Nizams and is known for the iconic Charminar and Golconda Fort · It is a major pharmaceutical and IT hub with HITEC City · The city is famous for Hyderabadi biryani and pearl trading, called the 'City of Pearls' · Hyderabad is the capital of Telangana with a population of over 10 million

desc: Ahmedabad is the largest city in Gujarat and a major industrial and commercial hub in western India. Founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmed Shah, the historic walled city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the first in India to receive this designation. The city is known for its Sabarmati Riverfront, the Sabarmati Ashram (Mahatma Gandhi's headquarters during the freedom struggle), and the intricate stepwells like Adalaj and Rani ki Vav. Ahmedabad is a major center for textile and pharmaceutical industries. It has a metropolitan population of over 7 million. The city is home to the world's largest cricket stadium, the Narendra Modi Stadium.
fact: Ahmedabad's historic walled city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the first in India · Founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmed Shah · The Sabarmati Ashram was Gandhi's headquarters during the freedom struggle · It is a major textile and pharmaceutical hub with 7 million population

desc: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is famously known as the 'Pink City' for the distinctive terracotta-pink color of its historic buildings. Founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, it was India's first planned city designed according to Vastu Shastra. The city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and part of the Golden Triangle tourist circuit alongside Delhi and Agra. Iconic landmarks include the Hawa Mahal, City Palace, Amber Fort, and Jantar Mantar astronomical observatory. Jaipur has a population of over 3 million and is a major center for traditional crafts including blue pottery, gemstone cutting, and block-printed textiles.
fact: Jaipur is the 'Pink City,' India's first planned city founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II · It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Golden Triangle tourist circuit · The Hawa Mahal, City Palace, Amber Fort, and Jantar Mantar are iconic landmarks · Jaipur is famous for blue pottery, gemstone cutting, and traditional Rajasthani textiles

desc: Pune is the second-largest city in Maharashtra and a major cultural, educational, and industrial hub. Known as the 'Oxford of the East,' Pune has more educational institutions per capita than any other Indian city. The city served as the seat of the Maratha Empire under the Peshwas and retains historic landmarks including the Shaniwar Wada fort, Aga Khan Palace, and Sinhagad Fort. Pune is a major automotive and manufacturing center, with companies like Tata Motors, Bajaj Auto, and Mercedes-Benz having manufacturing plants in the region. The city has a population of over 6 million and is known for its vibrant nightlife, food culture, and pleasant climate.
fact: Pune is known as the 'Oxford of the East' with the highest per capita concentration of educational institutions · It was the seat of the Maratha Empire under the Peshwas · It is a major automotive manufacturing hub with Tata Motors and Bajaj Auto · The city has historic landmarks including Shaniwar Wada and Aga Khan Palace

desc: Surat is a major port city in Gujarat and one of India's fastest-growing urban centers. It is the world's largest diamond cutting and polishing hub, handling over 90% of the world's rough diamonds. The city was a major trading port during the Mughal era, connecting India to Europe, Africa, and the Middle East. Surat is also a leading textile manufacturing center, earning it the nickname 'Textile City of India.' The city has a population of over 6 million and is known for its vibrant food culture, especially Surati Kathiawadi cuisine. The Diamonds Bourse in Surat is the world's largest diamond trading center.
fact: Surat is the world's largest diamond cutting and polishing hub, handling 90% of global rough diamonds · It is also a leading textile manufacturing center ('Textile City of India') · The city was a major Mughal-era trading port · The Diamonds Bourse is the world's largest diamond trading center
